A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RNG by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures and tables support comparison, including v4's three-page Supplementary Material. V1 has no separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original relighting experiments on real and synthetic scenes, comparisons with NRHints, and component ablations in Table 1 and Figures 6–10.

after.justification: V4 reports original point-light and environment-light relighting results, novel-view synthesis comparisons, and additional diagnostic experiments in the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: The stated lighting computation changes: v1 conditions its radiance decoder on intensity falloff G, whereas v4 describes decoding reflectance and subsequently multiplying by light intensity and falloff. The latent Gaussian representation, shadow cue, depth refinement and forward-deferred training procedure remain.

E1.justification: V4 expands beyond point-light relighting to novel environment-light relighting and static-environment novel-view synthesis. Tables 2–3 include additional scenes such as CupPlane, HairBlue, Ficus and Flowers. It also tests changing light distance and demonstrates a highly reflective failure case; v1's moving-light-direction demonstration is retained.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates NRHints as its external comparator. V4 adds GS3 to the corresponding point-light comparison, evaluates GS-IR and Relightable 3D Gaussian under environment lighting, and compares against vanilla 3DGS in supplementary Table 3.

E3.justification: New protocols include equal-view-count training under point lights for RNG versus unknown environment lighting for the environment-light baselines, followed by evaluation under a shared novel environment map. Supplementary NVS tests use forward-only RNG with shadow cues and depth refinement disabled. Network-size experiments vary width and hidden-layer count. The existing 512 × 512 resolution and 1000-view cap remain.

E4.justification: V4 adds network-size sensitivity tests, empirical forward-versus-deferred geometry/shadow comparisons, light-distance tests, depth-map diagnostics, a reflective failure case, and a neural-appearance versus spherical-harmonics comparison. The original component and depth-refinement ablations remain, while the moving-light-direction figure is relocated to the supplement.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, uncertainty bars, or significance tests. V4 retains point estimates and across-scene averages without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V4 adds results for the new comparisons and analyses and revises numerous Table 1 entries. For example, NRHints' WhiteFur PSNR changes from 30.1356 to 23.4099 while RNG's remains 33.7007. The condensed component-ablation figure retains PSNR but omits v1's SSIM/LPIPS entries. The revised baseline scores are unexplained and do not establish a same-setting improvement in RNG.

T1.justification: The decoder's mathematical definition changes from falloff-conditioned radiance in v1 Equations 6 and 9 to reflectance in v4 Equations 3 and 6, with subsequent intensity/falloff multiplication. V4's explicit multiplicative depth correction restates the linear, view-dependent scaling already described in v1. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The three central contributions and efficient relighting of hard-surface and soft-boundary objects remain. V4 adds the abstract/introduction claim of better shadows than concurrent GS3 and competitive efficiency with GS-based methods, extending v1's main comparison against NRHints.

C2.justification: V4 attributes environment-relighting advantages to point-lit inputs and neural appearance modeling, adds network size to its explanation of the NRHints quality-cost tradeoff, and makes the reflection limitation concrete through a failure case attributed to rasterization. The central geometry-dependent shadow limitation and forward/deferred interpretation remain.

D1.justification: V4 newly specifies 100k training steps, approximately 30k forward-shading steps, shadow-cue cache updates every five iterations, omission of refinement for shadow-camera depth, and black synthetic backgrounds. Its four-hidden-layer description clarifies v1's six-layer wording without establishing an architectural resize. Most existing optimizer, feature, encoding and hardware details remain.

R1.justification: V4 substantially repositions RNG relative to concurrent GS3, emphasizing shared capture conditions and differences in shadow quality and appearance assumptions. It also specifies RNA's synthetic-input and ground-truth-geometry requirements, adds Neural Reflectance Fields and IRON citations, and removes much of the broad NeRF and early image-based relighting survey.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method explanations are extensively rewritten, with revised terminology throughout. Implementation becomes a results subsection, experimental setup receives explicit organization, and supplementary Sections 6–7 reorganize supporting explanations and analyses. These changes substantially alter the narrative beyond scientific additions.

P2.justification: V4 changes the document layout, removes the opening teaser, redraws the pipeline and shadow/depth diagrams, combines real/synthetic comparisons, and restructures tables and ablation displays. It adds several diagnostic figures and two tables. V1 Figure 8 becomes supplementary Figure 14, while its forward/deferred diagram is redrawn as Figure 11.

improvement.justification: The directly relevant GS3 comparison and targeted tests of appearance representation, shading stages and network size substantially address v1's limited validation beyond NRHints. Added training details and a concrete reflective failure case improve reproducibility and applicability assessment. Different training illumination limits the environment comparison, and unexplained NRHints score revisions weaken its revised rankings, but the independent comparative and diagnostic evidence still substantially strengthens the paper.
